punchline: Nicholas Carr felt as if someone were tinkering with his brain: a page or two into a book, his mind drifted.
thirty_sec: Nicholas Carr noticed that his concentration slipped after a page or two. A blogger he quotes said he could no longer read War and Peace. Carr argues that the brain adapts to what we repeat, as it does in London taxi drivers who map the city, and that constant online skimming may be reshaping how we read.
